subject: Decision pack: visibility mergepoint for per-path economics & SLA exception flow
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Collins <sam.collins@apexanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Decision pack: visibility mergepoint for per-path economics & SLA exception flow

Team — attaching a short decision pack (v1) and a sample query export from a recent tenant spike. Apex (CC'd) has asked for clearer per-path cost and latency breakdowns plus a deterministic SLA-exception path they can rely on for bursty workloads.

Why this matters now:
- Apex is actively evaluating Dedicated; their procurement requires an operational view that ties token spend to specific API routes and fallback behavior.
- Current console tiles show aggregate spend and p50/p95 latency, but customers want sliceable attribution (by route + model variant) and a simple SLA-exception narrative we can point to in the contract.

Asks:
1) Product: decide the canonical set of path attributes we expose (route, model, quantization profile, tenant slice). I sketched a proposal in the attached PDF (pages 2–4).
2) Engineering: confirm feasibility and an estimated engineering cost for one-time backfill + realtime ingestion for the attributes above. Marcus, can you provide a short checklist of missing events/fields we need from the runtime?
3) Data/UX: minimal wire for a "slice explorer" that lets Apex pivot on route + model + token type (input/output). Rachel — can you scope low/med/high fidelity options?

Timeline: Procurement needs a statement of delivery (MVP or planned GA) by next week to keep the procurement review on track. I'd like a brief readout by EOD Thursday so I can share with Apex.

Attachments: decision-pack-v1.pdf (short deck), sample-query-results.csv (example token-by-route output).

Thanks — Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Decision pack: visibility mergepoint for per-path economics & SLA exception flow

Jasmine — thanks for the pack, skimmed the CSV. Quick technical notes: 

- What we have today: per-request metadata includes endpoint name, model id, seq_length, and kernel_type. The runtime emits token counts and observed latency per request, and we already sample KV-cache hits but not consistently tag quantization profile on every token row.
- Gaps for the proposal: we need (A) persistent route id (logical route key) surfaced in the runtime trace, (B) consistent model_variant tag (e.g., gpt-small-q4_0), and (C) token_role (input/output) at the token event level for accurate unit economics.

Engineering effort estimate (rough):
- Short term (MVP): 2 engineers · 2 weeks — add route-id + model_variant tags to the emission pipeline, augment ingestion schema, and add a backfill job for the last 30 days (best-effort).
- Medium term (robust): 3 engineers · 6 weeks — make tags enforced at the runtime compile step, add integration tests, and build a streaming pre-aggregator to avoid exploding storage for high-volume tenants.

Operational caveat: backfilling token-level detail for large tenants (Apex included) could be heavy; we should offer a 30-day backfill window as an explicit contract item. Also we should decide if we store raw token events or only pre-aggregates (per-route-per-tenant-per-minute).

I can draft a checklist of required runtime events by EOD tomorrow. For now, questions for Product: do we prefer raw event retention or pre-aggregates as the canonical field for the console? That choice affects both cost and response time for the slice explorer.

—Marcus
Lead Backend Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Collins <sam.collins@apexanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Oct 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Decision pack: visibility mergepoint for per-path economics & SLA exception flow

Thanks — concise framing. A few product/prioritization points: 

1) For the procurement ask, we should commit to an MVP that exposes per-route pre-aggregates (minute-level) and a documented SLA-exception playbook (what we will do if a path exceeds latency/failed-call thresholds). That keeps initial scope limited and aligns with procurement timelines.
2) If we offer raw token retention as an optional add-on for customers who need forensic capabilities, we can gate it behind a reserved-capacity contract (good upsell).
3) Decision: default to pre-aggregates for console (cost/latency) and offer a "forensics mode" for raw tokens. Marcus — that should reduce ingestion pressure but still give Apex the view they need.

Rachel — please prioritize a low-fidelity mock that demonstrates (A) pivot-by-route, (B) time-series cost stack, (C) SLA-exception timeline (what rolled to fallback/variant). I think a single-pane drilldown with a CSV export is enough for procurement.

Jasmine — I'll own the procurement note and add the backfill window to the contract language if we confirm the 30-day limit. I will also draft the one-paragraph SLA-exception statement for Apex to include in their procurement docs.

Kimberly Park
Sr PM, Pricing & Packaging
Redwood Inference
From: Sam Collins <sam.collins@apexanalytics.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 8 Oct 2027 15:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Decision pack: visibility mergepoint for per-path economics & SLA exception flow

Appreciate the quick turnaround and pragmatic proposal. A couple clarifications from our procurement/security team: 

- The 30-day backfill window is acceptable as an initial condition — can we please have a short paragraph in the contract that states exactly what is backfilled (fields included) and the expected latency of the backfilled dataset once ready?
- For SLA-exception flow: we need a clear escalation contact and a runbook excerpt that says when Redwood will move traffic to fallback model variants vs. queue vs. reject. Even a table of thresholds (e.g., p95 latency > 2s for > 5m) and the corresponding action would be sufficient for our team to move forward.

We’re ready to sign the NDA + LOI once we have the procurement paragraph and the short SLA playbook. Thanks — looking forward to the MVP demo.

Sam Collins
Head of Platform Ops
Apex Analytics
